migration.description: Persist hourly prefix reservation authority and assign existing conversation ceilings exclusively to the range manager.
migration.release_unit_description: Backend PR1 allocation correction before PR2 API and frontend integration.

durable_state.description: Conversation identities, reservation ceilings, hourly prefix ownership, retained invocation IDs, and pending terminal journal identities.
durable_state.storage_implementation: Existing business SQLite database and existing terminal journal; no new allocation files or conversation mapping table.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Supported 2.x business databases accepted by the existing schema/materialization path, with fixtures for pre-master structure, 2.85.1 partial staging, and 2.85.4 single-sequence allocation state.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: The next allocation-correction release; numeric version is not assigned by this planning record.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Idempotently create hourly_invoke_prefixes with Unix-hour primary key, unique six-character prefix, ceiling bounds -1 through 923520, and UTC audit timestamps; record an immutable completion marker in the existing migration registry atomically.

dml_changes.description: Recover conversation floors on demand from the durable ceiling and known retained/pending issued suffixes; create or recover the current hourly owner; commit 64-sequence batches before publication. Statistics writes must not overwrite ceilings.

database_migration.historical_data_reason: No invocation IDs are rewritten, no unreliable UTC-hour ownership is inferred for legacy unbound prefixes, and no global history scan is added at startup. Existing statistics materialization remains a separate resumable operation.

progress_signals: Schema operation identity and committed marker outcome.
Owner type, generated identity, UTC hour, generation, recovered floor, range bounds, and commit/publication result.
Separate existing statistics phase, cursor, queue count, aggregate freshness, and completion signals.
Cache seed source and row bound, target/occupancy, memory-only resizing, admission timeout, return outcome, and lifecycle release.
pause_points: Before schema installation and after its atomic commit; interrupted installation leaves no partial completion marker.
Between committed owner reservation batches; never publish an uncommitted range.
Between existing committed historical materialization pages, independently of allocator operations.

executed_test_evidence: src/tests/stateful_sqlite/invocation_ranges.rs: atomic marker/DDL rollback and reentry, legacy live-floor preservation, committed-range restart, allocator-exclusive ceiling and pending namespace recovery.
src/tests/archive_file_io/prompt_cache_control_file_lock.rs: real SQLite worker drain after timed-out return, followed by safe replacement generation.
Current-candidate full resource profiles and Linux service evidence are required by IMPLEMENTATION.md and the delivery report; package regressions alone do not certify readiness.

required_test_evidence: Not the selected impact: previous per-invocation and volatile-hour writers do not implement the new durable ownership contract.
Existing public API response fields and compact ID shape remain compatible.
Candidate reads and writes supported earlier-Minor fixtures, preserving historical IDs, partial materialization state, and known sequence floors.
Schema interruption and reentry are idempotent; marker identity is immutable.
Crash after range commit but before publication skips the committed range; same-hour restart recovers its prefix.
Forward-repair code handles state left after schema commit, reservation commit, and interrupted lifecycle release.
Earlier-Minor allocation writers are not required to write the migrated reservation state.
Not selected; no new direct-major-skipping compatibility is introduced.
